A delightful discovery off bustling Ben Thanh Market
Feb 2019 • Family
Our tour guide during our recent port of call at Phu My for HCMC took us to this fantastic find. It looks unassuming on the outside--you have to walk past numerous nail salons/vendors before you take the tricky steps up to the rustic nicely-decorated dining room. The food--the rice cakes, beef pho, stuffed escargots, fried spring rolls, among a few others from the extensive menu--was delicious and full of flavor. Service was quick and efficient, and the place was clean. If you're looking for a restaurant that serves excellent regional Vietnamese cuisine, good value for money, frequented by locals, and away from the hoards of tourists, then this is a place to check out.

reviews.review_text:

Los Angeles, California12 contributions

Do not miss this restaurant!
Jan 2013 • Couples
The main picture for this restaurant is not the correct one. Others later on in the visitor photo list are correct. Restaurant is hard to find, but is worth it once you find it. Enlist the help of a local if necessary. We were only in Saigon for a week but came here for dinner twice because it was just sooooo good.

If they stick you in the room to the right of the main dining area, note that the ceiling is low and the AC may not reach your table, so you may have a sweaty dining experience. Just order some cold bababa (333) and sweat through what is about to be an awesome dining experience!

There are entrees in this restaurant, but it's more fun to order several small plates/appetizers off of the left side of the menu. Be sure to order the pancakes with shrimp bits on top - they are amazing! The ground chili sauce is not to be trifled with, but is an excellent complement to the food if you enjoy spice. Other can't-misses are the banana leaf-wrapped rice and meat concoctions and, of course, the different varieties of spring rolls. Here you can have a huge feast and 2-3 beers for about $7-8US per person. My husband walked out of the restaurant and proclaimed that he didn't deserve the amazing meal we'd just had. It's just. that. good. GO!

Hidden Gem by Ben Thanh
Jul 2012 • Couples
Visited this local spot a few times, after it was suggested by a local we worked with. If you are in Vietnam trying Hue style (both royal and traditional) dishes is a must. Here is a good place to start. The food is excellent as is the price. Keep in mind the portions are smaller so between two people ordering 3 or 4 dishes should be just about right. Finding the place is a small task but worth it. Also as other reviews pointed out, the service, especially during the peak hours, is pretty slow, as if the service hasn't been trained or just aren't on the same page, leaving you wondering if they want to take your order or if your order will ever come, but it does. And they are still friendly. For example one of the visits, the staff was very attentive and went out of their way to serve a family with a teen with special needs. It was very sweet and touching to watch. We also experienced them cleaning up and putting up chairs as we were still eating, which as a westerner seems a little rude I guess, but when in Rome... Go for the food it's worth it!

Myself and spouse arrived at at 8.30pm. There were about 4 to 6 other tables occupied. Noted that the greeter did not seem too happy to see us. One of the staff (lady manager/owner?) was actually drying her just washed long hair by the fan in the dining hall. Feels that the place were about to close even though I was informed it closes at 10pm. My waitress was also rather surly. I think she just wants us out of the place so that she could go elsewhere.

4 of the dishes we wanted were sold out. Fortunately the ordered 4 that was available was delicious, and they were also very generous servings. I could imagine that the the sold out dishes must have been even tastier.

BTW, Rat in "Rat Hue" translates to "Real." No rodents that I can see here, but feels that they may come out after the place is closed for the night. 3 to 5 years ago, this must have been a fine dining place judging by decor. But now it is left with faded tablecloths, stained seats on expensive chairs, and chipped plates.

Next time when I am back in HCMC, I will visit for lunch. The food deserves a repeat visit. And hopefully the service will be better. As for the decor, well.....
